meal.title: Why Every C Statement Ends with a Semicolon
meal.objective: Explain why each statement must end with a semicolon and how execution order follows those marks

voice.script: What if I told you a single tiny mark controls everything you write? Every instruction in C must end with a semicolon, which tells the compiler where one command stops and the next begins. Here’s a tiny program that shows two statements. When you run it, the number 5 appears, proving the statements ran in order. Imagine a flow line where each block ends with a semicolon. Remember: the semicolon marks the end of each statement. Add another printf after the first one and end it with a semicolon.
